paragraphs: Aldeyra Therapeutics is a biotechnology company devoted to discovering innovative therapies designed to treat immune-mediated diseases. Our approach is to develop pharmaceuticals that modulate protein systems, instead of directly inhibiting or activating single protein targets, with the goal of optimizing multiple pathways at once while minimizing toxicity. Our product candidates include RASP (reactive aldehyde species) modulators ADX-248, ADX-246, and chemically related molecules for the potential treatment of systemic and retinal immune-mediated diseases. Our late-stage product candidates are reproxalap, a RASP modulator for the potential treatment of dry eye disease and allergic conjunctivitis, and ADX-2191, a novel formulation of intravitreal methotrexate for the potential treatment of primary vitreoretinal lymphoma and retinitis pigmentosa.
Our development pipeline, as of the date of filing of this annual report on Form 10-K is illustrated below.

On October 31, 2023 (the AbbVie Option Agreement Effective Date), we entered into an exclusive option agreement (the AbbVie Option Agreement) with AbbVie Inc. (AbbVie), pursuant to which we granted AbbVie an exclusive option (the AbbVie Option) to obtain (a) a co-exclusive license in the United States to facilitate a collaboration with us to develop, manufacture and commercialize reproxalap in the United States, (b) an exclusive license to develop, manufacture, and commercialize reproxalap outside the United States, (c) a right of first negotiation for compounds that are owned or otherwise controlled by us in the field of ophthalmology relating to treating conditions of the ocular surface, and (d) a right to review data for any other compounds that are owned or otherwise controlled by us in the fields of ophthalmology and immunology before such data is shared with any other third party (the Collaboration Agreement). AbbVie has paid us a non-refundable payment of $1.0 million in consideration of the AbbVie Option (the AbbVie Option Payment).

On December 21, 2023, pursuant to the AbbVie Option Agreement, AbbVie extended the period during which it may exercise the AbbVie Option by paying us a non-refundable payment of $5.0 million (the AbbVie Option Extension Fee). If the Collaboration Agreement is entered into, the AbbVie Option Payment and the AbbVie Option Extension Fee will be credited against the upfront cash payment payable by AbbVie.

On November 15, 2024, we entered into the Expansion Side Letter (the Expansion Letter) with AbbVie. The Expansion Letter makes certain changes to the AbbVie Option Agreement, among other things, providing that we will conduct certain launch activities, which costs shall not exceed mid-single-digit millions of dollars without AbbVie's approval, and which costs will be considered allowable expenses pursuant to the Collaboration Agreement upon the delivery of AbbVie's written notice of exercising the AbbVie Option and entry into the Collaboration Agreement, such that 60% of our allowable expenses will be reimbursed by AbbVie in the event of exercise. If AbbVie does not deliver a written notice of exercising the AbbVie Option and we do not execute the Collaboration Agreement, we will remain solely responsible for such costs. AbbVie has also independently initiated pre-commercialization planning activities. In addition, the Exercise Period (as defined in the AbbVie Option Agreement) was restricted to ten (10) business days following the date, if any, that we receive approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration of the NDA for reproxalap in dry eye disease (the FDA Decision), provided that AbbVie shall provide us notice in case AbbVie determines that it will not exercise the AbbVie Option.

Upon AbbVie's delivery of the agreement execution notice and the parties entering into the Collaboration Agreement, AbbVie would pay us a $100.0 million upfront cash payment, less the AbbVie Option Payment and the AbbVie Option Extension Fee. In addition, we would be eligible to receive up to approximately $300.0 million in regulatory and commercial milestone payments, inclusive of a $100.0 million milestone payment payable if the FDA Decision is received prior to or after the execution of the Collaboration Agreement. In the United States, we would share profits and losses with AbbVie from the commercialization of reproxalap according to a split of 60% for AbbVie and 40% for us. Outside of the United States, we would be eligible to receive tiered royalties on net sales of reproxalap. As of February 27, 2026, AbbVie has not exercised the AbbVie Option.

All of our development plans and timelines are subject to adjustment depending on recruitment rate, regulatory review, preclinical and clinical results, funding, and other factors that could delay the initiation, completion, or reporting of clinical trials. Regulatory review timelines are flexible and subject to change based on the regulator's workload and other potential review issues. The timing of ongoing clinical trials depends, in part, on the availability of clinical research facilities and staffing, and the ability to recruit patients.
As we continue to execute on our strategy of expanding our product candidate pipeline, we may license or acquire new immune-modulating approaches with novel therapeutic potential.

We have no products approved for sale in the United States or elsewhere. We will not receive any revenue from sales of our product candidates that we develop until we obtain regulatory approval. We intend to commercialize our products, if approved for sale, directly or through collaborations. Although we may receive commercial and license revenue in the future, we have to date primarily funded our operations through the sale of our common stock, convertible preferred stock, convertible promissory notes, warrants, and borrowings under debt facilities. We will need to raise additional capital in the form of debt or equity or through partnerships to fund additional development of our product candidates, and we may in-license, acquire, or invest in complementary businesses or products. In addition, contingent on capital resources, we may augment, diminish, or otherwise modify the clinical development plan described herein.

Since our incorporation, we have devoted substantially all of our resources to the preclinical and clinical development of our product candidates. If we do obtain marketing approval for reproxalap or any other product candidate that we develop, we intend to partner with other companies for commercialization, though there can be no guarantee that such partnership will be available. Our ability to generate revenues, if any, largely depends upon our ability, alone or with others, to complete development of and obtain regulatory approvals for our product candidates, and to successfully manufacture, market, and sell our products. The results of our operations will vary significantly from year-to-year and quarter-to-quarter, and depend on a number of factors, including risks related to our business and industry, risks relating to intellectual property and other legal matters, risks related to our common stock, and other risks that are detailed in the section of this annual report on Form 10-K entitled "Risk Factors".

In response to infection, injury, endogenous and exogenous chemical triggers, heat, and other stimuli, RASP (reactive aldehyde species) are generated through a variety of metabolic processes, including alcohol oxidation, enzymatic and non-enzymatic lipid oxidation, and polyamine and sphingosine metabolism. RASP appear to effect inflammation signaling via covalent binding to thiol (sulfur-containing) and amine (nitrogen-containing) residues on proteins, including receptors and enzymes. RASP-protein adducts directly influence the function of proteins, leading to activation of intracellular inflammatory factors, including NF‑κB, an important mediator in the inflammatory response, and inflammasomes. In addition, RASP adducts bind to Scavenger Receptor A, which also initiates pro-inflammatory signaling and leads to the formation of antibodies against the adducted protein, at least in part explaining the presence of host-directed antibodies in autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis. Levels of RASP are generally observed to be elevated in ocular and systemic inflammatory disease, including the diseases represented in our RASP modulator pipeline, and thus represent therapeutic targets for immune modulation. RASP are also associated with metabolic and neurodegenerative diseases, and, in addition to upregulating inflammation, lead to DNA damage, accumulation of metabolic aggregates, and other pathologic manifestations.

Because of the inherent toxicity of RASP, most, if not all, living organisms contain enzymes, such as aldehyde reductases and aldehyde dehydrogenases, that convert RASP into non-toxic molecules. Genetic mutations in the RASP-metabolizing enzymes cause disease. In Sjögren-Larsson Syndrome, for example, mutations in fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase are responsible for skin, neurological, and retinal disease.

Aside from the potentiation of inflammation, there is no generally accepted biological role of high levels of RASP. Some physiologic molecules have RASP forms, including retinaldehyde (a form of Vitamin A) and pyridoxal and pyridoxal phosphate (forms of Vitamin B6), but the activity of physiological RASP is highly restricted by chaperone and other proteins that prevent reaction with other molecules, including our RASP modulators. Thus, pharmacotherapeutic RASP modulation is expected not to adversely affect normal physiologic processes. Consistent with the lack of accessibility of physiologic RASP, our most advanced RASP modulator, reproxalap, which has been administered as an ophthalmic solution to approximately 2,700 patients across a number of completed clinical trials for up to 12 months, has been observed to be generally well tolerated and has not been associated with any serious adverse events; mild and transient instillation site irritation is the most commonly reported adverse event in clinical trials. Similarly, an orally administered RASP modulator, ADX‑629, which has been administered to more than 180 patients across a number of Phase 1 and Phase 2 clinical trials for up to 90 days, has been observed to be generally well tolerated and has not been associated with any serious adverse events.

Because RASP affect many proteins simultaneously, the RASP modulator platform represents a unique and novel pharmacologic approach that, unlike almost all drugs in use today, is not designed to directly inhibit or activate a particular protein but instead targets a family of small molecules that in turn affect the activity and structure of many proteins at once. RASP modulation, therefore, has the potential to down-regulate pro-inflammatory systems or groups of proteins, and may lead to multiple beneficial clinical effects while avoiding toxicity associated with single-target inhibition or activation.

paragraphs: Our business is subject to numerous risks. You should carefully consider the risks described below together with the other information set forth in this annual report on Form 10-K, which could materially affect our business, financial condition, and future results. The risks described below are not the only risks facing our company. Risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently deem to be immaterial also may materially adversely affect our business, prospects, financial condition, and operating results.

Below is a summary of the principal factors that make an investment in our common stock speculative or risky. The risk factor summary does not address all of the risks that we face. Additional discussion of the risks summarized in the risk factor summary, and other risks that we face, can be found below and should be carefully considered, together with other information in this annual report on Form 10-K and our other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission before making investment decisions regarding our common stock.

• Our business is dependent in large part on the successful commercialization of reproxalap. If we are unable to successfully obtain marketing approval for reproxalap, or experience significant delays in doing so, or if, after obtaining marketing approval, we or our strategic partners fail to successfully commercialize reproxalap, our business will be materially harmed.

• To generate revenue, we will depend on FDA approval and successful commercialization of reproxalap. Our success in obtaining regulatory approval of reproxalap from the FDA depends on whether we successfully address the issues raised by the FDA in the reproxalap Complete Response Letters, and our ability to address any issues the FDA may raise in the future. If we are unable to successfully obtain FDA approval, or FDA approval is delayed or limited, our ability to generate revenue will be significantly delayed.

• If we remain responsible for funding further development and commercialization of reproxalap, we may be unable to raise the additional capital required to further develop and commercialize reproxalap or enter into a collaboration agreement with another pharmaceutical company with equivalent or comparable terms, or at all.
• If we fail to develop and commercialize other product candidates, we may be unable to grow our business.

We previously developed ADX‑2191 for the treatment of proliferative vitreoretinopathy pursuant to an Exclusive License Agreement with Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary (MEEI), originally entered into in July 2016 between MEEI and Helio Vision, Inc. (Helio), as amended, (the MEEI Agreement). We assumed the MEEI Agreement in connection with our 2019 acquisition of Helio.

Pursuant to the MEEI Agreement, we obtained an exclusive, worldwide license from MEEI to develop and commercialize ADX‑2191 under certain patents and patent applications, in addition to other licenses to intellectual property (the MEEI Patent Rights). We have agreed to use our commercially reasonable efforts to develop ADX‑2191 and to meet certain specified effort and achievement benchmarks by certain dates.

In consideration for the rights licensed under the MEEI Agreement, Helio issued MEEI a number of shares of its preferred stock and Helio agreed, during the term of the MEEI Agreement, to pay non-creditable non-refundable license maintenance fees to MEEI of $15,000 on each of the second and third anniversary of the MEEI Agreement, $25,000 on each of the fourth and fifth anniversary of the MEEI Agreement and $35,000 on the sixth and each subsequent anniversary of the MEEI Agreement. In addition, Helio was obligated to make future sales-dependent milestone payments to MEEI of up to the low seven figures in the aggregate, as well as royalty payments to MEEI at a rate which, as a percentage of net sales, is in the low single digits for products that incorporate or use the MEEI Patent Rights. Helio is also obligated under the MEEI Agreement to pay MEEI a percentage of certain sublicense revenue at a percentage rate that descends from low-double digits to mid-single digits based on the date of the sublicense. Following our acquisition of Helio, we became obligated to make any future payments previously owed by Helio under the MEEI Agreement. There is no additional equity consideration issuable under the MEEI Agreement.

paragraphs: Aldeyra Therapeutics 為一間生物科技公司，專注於發現創新療法，用以治療免疫介導性疾病。我們的策略為開發可以調節蛋白質系統的藥物，而非直接抑制或活化單一蛋白質目標，目標為同時優化多種路徑，同時降低毒性。我們的產品候選藥物包括 RASP（反應醛類物質）調節劑 ADX-248、ADX-246，以及與其化學相關的分子，用以潛在治療全身性及視網膜免疫介導性疾病。我們的晚期產品候選藥物為 reproxalap，一種 RASP 調節劑，用以潛在治療乾眼症及過敏性結膜炎，以及 ADX-2191，一種新型的玻璃體內甲氨蝶呤製劑，用以潛在治療原發性玻璃體視網膜淋巴瘤及視網膜色素變異症。
我們的開發管道，截至本年度報告 10-K 申報日為止，如下圖所示。

於 2023 年 10 月 31 日（AbbVie 選項協議生效日），我們與 AbbVie Inc.（AbbVie）簽訂一項獨家選項協議（AbbVie 選項協議），根據該協議，我們授予 AbbVie 一項獨家選項（AbbVie 選項），以取得（a）美國獨家授權，用以與我們合作開發、製造及商業化 reproxalap 在美國，（b）美國以外地區的獨家授權，用以開發、製造及商業化 reproxalap，在美國以外地區，（c）針對我們擁有或由我們控制的、用以治療角膜表面疾病的 ophthalmology 領域化合物的首優先談判權，以及（d）針對我們擁有或由我們控制的、用以治療 ophthalmology 及 immunology 領域的其他化合物的資料審閱權，於此資料與任何其他第三方分享前（Collaboration Agreement）。AbbVie 已支付我們一筆不可退款的 1.0 百萬美元，作為 AbbVie 選項的對價（AbbVie 選項付款）。
於 2023 年 12 月 21 日，根據 AbbVie 選項協議，AbbVie 以支付我們一筆不可退款的 5.0 百萬美元（AbbVie 選項延長費用）來延長其行使 AbbVie 選項的期間。若 Collaboration Agreement 籤訂，則 AbbVie 選項付款及 AbbVie 選項延長費用將抵銷 AbbVie 需支付的初始現金對價。

於 2024 年 11 月 15 日，本公司與 AbbVie 簽訂 Expansion Side Letter（Expansion Letter）。Expansion Letter 對 AbbVie Option Agreement 進行若干變更，包括本公司將執行某些發售活動，其費用在未經 AbbVie 同意前不得超過中位數單位數百萬美元，且在 AbbVie 交付書面行使 AbbVie Option 通知並簽訂 Collaboration Agreement 後，該費用將被視為 Collaboration Agreement 所允許的費用，使得在 AbbVie 行使 Option 情況下，本公司可獲得 60% 的允許費用補償。若 AbbVie 未交付書面行使 AbbVie Option 通知，且本公司未簽訂 Collaboration Agreement，本公司將獨自承擔該費用。AbbVie 亦已獨立啟動預商業化規劃活動。此外，Exercise Period（如 AbbVie Option Agreement 所定義）限制為自本公司收到美國食品藥物管理局（U.S. Food and Drug Administration）關於 reproxalap 在乾眼症（dry eye disease）新藥申請（NDA）之核准通知（FDA Decision）之日起十（10）個營業日，但 AbbVie 應在決定不行使 AbbVie Option 時通知本公司。

於 AbbVie 交付協議簽訂通知並雙方簽訂 Collaboration Agreement 後，AbbVie 將支付本公司 100.0 百萬美元現金預付款，扣除 AbbVie Option Payment 及 AbbVie Option Extension Fee。此外，本公司將有資格獲得最高約 300.0 百萬美元的監管與商業里程碑付款，包括若於 Collaboration Agreement 簽訂前或後收到 FDA Decision 時支付 100.0 百萬美元的里程碑付款。於美國，本公司將根據 60% 給 AbbVie、40% 給本公司之比例與 AbbVie 共享 reproxalap 商業化之利潤與損失。於美國以外地區，本公司將有資格獲得 reproxalap 淨銷售額之階梯式版稅。截至 2026 年 2 月 27 日，AbbVie 尚未行使 AbbVie Option。
本公司所有開發計畫與時程皆可能根據招募率、監管審查、前臨牀與臨牀結果、資金及其他可能延誤臨牀試驗啟動、完成或報告之因素而調整。監管審查時程具有彈性，並可能根據監管機構工作負荷及其他潛在審查問題而變更。持續進行之臨牀試驗時程部分取決於臨牀研究設施與人力之可得性，以及招募病患之能力。
隨著本公司持續執行擴展產品候選藥物管線之策略，本公司可能授權或收購具新治療潛力之新免疫調節方法。

本公司目前尚無產品獲得美國或其他國家的銷售許可。本公司將不會從銷售我們開發的產品候選品中獲得任何收入，直到我們取得相關監管批准為止。本公司預計在獲得銷售許可後，將直接或透過合作夥伴進行產品商業化。雖然本公司未來可能獲得商業及授權收入，但截至目前為止，本公司主要透過銷售普通股、可轉換優先股、可轉換貸款憑證、權證及債務融資來資助營運。本公司將需要透過債務或股權融資，或透過合作夥伴來籌措額外資金，以資助產品候選品的進一步開發，並可能透過授權、收購或投資來補強、取得或投資於補充性業務或產品。此外，視資金資源而定，本公司可能調整、減少或以其他方式修改 herein 所述的臨牀開發計畫。

自本公司設立以來，我們已將幾乎所有資源投入產品候選品的前期臨牀及臨牀開發。若我們獲得 reproxalap 或任何其他產品候選品的市場批准，我們預計將與其他公司合作進行商業化，但無法保證此類合作將可取得。我們能否產生收入，若有的話， largely 取決於我們能否，單獨或與他人合作，完成產品候選品的開發並取得相關監管批准，以及成功製造、行銷及銷售我們的產品。我們的營運結果將會因年與年、季與季之間的差異而大幅變動，並取決於許多因素，包括與我們業務及產業相關的風險、與智慧財產權及其他法律事項相關的風險、與我們普通股相關的風險，以及其他在本年度報告 10-K 表單中「風險因素」部分詳細說明的風險。

在對感染、傷害、內源性及外源性化學觸發劑、熱度及其他刺激反應時，RASP（反應醛類物質）會透過多種代謝過程產生，包括酒精氧化、酵素及非酵素脂質氧化，以及多胺及鞘氨醇代謝。RASP 似乎透過與蛋白質上的硫醇（含硫）及胺基（含氮）殘基進行共價結合，來影響發炎訊號。RASP-蛋白質加成物會直接影響蛋白質的功能，導致活化細胞內的發炎因子，包括 NF-κB，這是發炎反應中的重要媒介，以及 inflammasomes。此外，RASP 加成物會與 Scavenger Receptor A 結合，也會啟動促發炎訊號，並導致針對加成蛋白產生抗體，至少部分解釋了自身免疫疾病如類風濕性關節炎中宿主導抗體的存在。RASP 的水平通常在眼睛及全身發炎性疾病中觀察到升高，包括我們 RASP 調節劑管線中所代表的疾病，因此代表免疫調節的治療目標。RASP 也與代謝及神經退化性疾病相關，除了會促進發炎外，還會導致 DNA 損傷、代謝聚合物的累積，以及其他病態表現。
由於 RASP 的固有毒性，大多數，如果說不是所有，生物體都含有將 RASP 轉換為無毒分子的酵素，例如醛還原酶及醛脫氫酶。RASP 代謝酵素的遺傳變異會導致疾病。例如，在 Sjögren-Larsson 綜合症中，脂肪醛脫氫酶的變異會導致皮膚、神經及視網膜疾病。

除了促進發炎外，目前尚無被廣泛接受的高 RASP 水平的生物功能。一些生理分子具有 RASP 形式，包括視黃醇（維生素 A 的一種形式）及吡哆醛和吡哆醛磷酸（維生素 B6 的一種形式），但生理性的 RASP 活性會受到載體及其他蛋白質的嚴格限制，以防止與其他分子反應，包括我們的 RASP 調節劑。因此，藥物治療性的 RASP 調節預期不會對正常的生理過程造成不利影響。根據生理 RASP 的不可接近性，我們最進展的 RASP 調節劑 reproxalap，已作為眼藥水形式給予約 2,700 名患者，進行多項已完成的臨牀試驗，持續時間達 12 個月，觀察到其通常耐受性良好，且未與任何嚴重不良事件相關；輕微且暫時的滴眼部位刺激是臨牀試驗中最常報告的不良事件。同樣地，一種口服的 RASP 調節劑 ADX-629，已給予超過 180 名患者，進行多項一期及二期臨牀試驗，持續時間達 90 天，觀察到其通常耐受性良好，且未與任何嚴重不良事件相關。
由於 RASP 會同時影響許多蛋白質，RASP 調節劑平台代表了一種獨特且創新藥物治療方法，與目前幾乎所有藥物不同，它並不是設計用來直接抑制或活化特定蛋白質，而是針對一組小分子，這些分子會同時影響許多蛋白質的活性及結構。因此，RASP 調節有潛力降低促發炎系統或蛋白質羣組，並可能導致多種臨牀益處，同時避免單一目標抑制或活化所導致的毒性。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，並與我們之財務報表及附於本年度10-K表報末尾之相關附註一併參考。本討論與分析中包含之部分資訊，包括有關我們業務與策略之資訊，包含風險、不確定性及假設之預測性陳述。您應閱讀本年度10-K表報中之「風險因素」及「預測性陳述特別說明」部分，以瞭解可能導致實際結果與下列討論與分析中所述或暗示之預測性陳述所描述結果有重大差異之重要因素。

我們是一家專注於發現與開發創新療法之生物科技公司，這些療法旨在治療免疫介導性疾病。我們的策略是開發能調節蛋白質系統之藥物，而非直接抑制或活化單一蛋白質目標，目標為同時優化多條路徑，同時降低毒性。我們之產品候選藥物包括RASP（反應醛類物質）調節劑ADX-248、ADX-246，以及化學相關分子，用於治療系統性及視網膜免疫介導性疾病。我們之晚期產品候選藥物為reproxalap，一種RASP調節劑，用於治療乾眼症及過敏性結膜炎，以及ADX-2191，一種新型玻璃體內甲氨蝶呤製劑，用於治療原發性玻璃體視網膜淋巴瘤及視網膜色素變性疾病。

自我們成立以來，我們已將幾乎所有資源投入於產品候選藥物之臨牀前及臨牀開發。我們產生收入的能力 largely 取決於我們單獨或與他人合作完成產品候選藥物之開發，以獲得監管批准，並製造、行銷及銷售產品候選藥物之能力。我們之營運結果將會每年及每季大幅變動，並取決於多項因素，包括與我們業務及產業相關之風險、智慧財產權及其他法律事項相關之風險、與我們普通股相關之風險，及其他在本年度10-K表報中「風險因素」部分詳細說明之風險。

2019 年 3 月，本公司與 Hercules 籤訂信用貸款協議，該協議提供最高 60.0 百萬美元的定期貸款，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，已撥款 15.0 百萬美元。經修正後的 Hercules 信用貸款協議規定，貸款人於 2026 年 4 月 1 日前僅需支付利息；(ii) 期限為 2026 年 4 月 1 日；(iii) 利率為 (a) Hercules 信用貸款協議中定義的 Prime Rate 加 3.10%，或 (b) 11.10% 中的較高者。經修正後的 Hercules 信用貸款協議內容，請參閱本 10-K 年度報告所附財務會計明細表之第九節。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，Hercules 信用貸款協議下尚有 15.0 百萬美元貸款餘額，且無餘額可供貸款。

2024年8月，我們與Jefferies簽訂公開市場銷售協議（Open Market Sales Agreement SM），委任Jefferies為銷售代理（2024 Jefferies Sales Agreement），我們可透過Jefferies不時發行及銷售普通股，總銷售所得上限為75.0 百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，尚無根據2024 Jefferies Sales Agreement之銷售交易。
我們將需要以債務或股權形式籌措額外資金，或透過合作關係，以資助產品候選藥物之進一步開發，並在獲得監管批准（如有）之情況下進行產品候選藥物之商業化。我們可能也會進授權、收購或投資於補充性業務或產品。此外，隨著資金資源允許，我們可能調整或修改 herein 所述之臨牀開發計畫。然而，任何資本市場之幹擾可能使任何融資更具挑戰性，且無法保證我們能以商業合理條件或任何方式籌措資金。

2023年10月31日（AbbVie Option Agreement生效日），我們與AbbVie Inc.（AbbVie）簽訂獨家選擇權協議（AbbVie Option Agreement），我們授予AbbVie獨家選擇權（AbbVie Option），以取得（a）美國獨家授權，與我們合作開發、製造及商業化reproxalap於美國，（b）美國以外地區之獨家授權，開發、製造及商業化reproxalap，（c）對我們擁有或由我們控制之眼科學領域化合物之優先談判權，用於治療角膜表面疾病，以及（d）在眼科學及免疫學領域，對我們擁有或由我們控制之任何其他化合物之數據審查權，於與任何其他第三方分享前（Collaboration Agreement）。AbbVie已支付我們1.0 百萬美元不可退款之金額作為AbbVie Option之對價（AbbVie Option Payment）。
AbbVie已支付我們1.0 百萬美元不可退款之金額作為AbbVie Option之對價（AbbVie Option Payment）。
於 2023 年 12 月 21 日，根據 AbbVie 選項協議，AbbVie 透過支付我們一筆不可退款的 5.0 百萬美元（即 AbbVie 選項延長費）來延長其行使 AbbVie 選項的期間。若合作協議已簽訂，則 AbbVie 選項付款與 AbbVie 選項延長費將抵銷 AbbVie 須支付的 upfront 現金款項。

於 2024 年 11 月 15 日，我們與 AbbVie 簽訂擴張附屬協議（Expansion Letter）。擴張附屬協議對 AbbVie 選項協議進行若干變更，包括我們將執行某些發售活動，其費用在未經 AbbVie 同意的情況下，不得超過中位數單位數百萬美元，且在 AbbVie 發出書面行使 AbbVie 選項通知並簽訂合作協議後，將被視為可報銷費用，如此時 AbbVie 行使選項，則我們可報銷費用的 60% 將由 AbbVie 補償。若 AbbVie 未發出書面行使 AbbVie 選項的通知，且我們未簽訂合作協議，則我們將獨自承擔此費用。AbbVie 也已獨立啟動預商業化規劃活動。此外，Exercise Period（如 AbbVie 選項協議所定義）被限制為在任何我們收到美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准 NDA 的日期後的十（10）個營業日，前提是 AbbVie 若決定不行使 AbbVie 選項，應通知我們。

在 AbbVie 發出協議簽訂通知且雙方簽訂合作協議後，AbbVie 將支付我們一筆 upfront 現金款項為 100.0 百萬美元，扣除 AbbVie 選項付款與 AbbVie 選項延長費。此外，我們將有資格獲得最高約 300.0 百萬美元的監管與商業里程碑付款，包括若 FDA 決定在合作協議簽訂前或後收到，則支付一筆 100.0 百萬美元的里程碑付款。在美國，我們將根據 60% 給 AbbVie、40% 給我們的比例，與 AbbVie 共享 reproxalap 的營運利潤與損失。在美國以外地區，我們將有資格根據淨銷售額獲得 tiered  royalty。截至 2026 年 2 月 27 日，AbbVie 尚未行使 AbbVie 選項。

我們先前為治療增生性玻璃體視網膜病變而開發 ADX‑2191，根據與麻省眼耳醫院（Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary，MEEI）簽訂的獨家授權協議（MEEI 協議）。該協議最初於 2016 年 7 月由 MEEI 與 Helio Vision, Inc.（Helio）簽訂，後經修正（MEEI 協議）。我們在 2019 年收購 Helio 時，接續了 MEEI 協議。
根據 MEEI 協議，我們從 MEEI 獲得獨家、全球性授權，以在特定專利與專利申請的基礎上開發與商業化 ADX‑2191，並取得其他智慧財產權（MEEI 專利權）。我們同意以商業上合理的努力開發 ADX‑2191，並在特定日期前達成特定努力與成就指標。

作為取得 MEEI 協議授權的對價，Helio 向 MEEI 發行若干優先股，且在 MEEI 協議的期限內，Helio 同意支付不可抵銷且不可退款的授權維護費用給 MEEI，於 MEEI 協議的第二與第三週年時各支付 15,000 美元，第四與第五週年時各支付 25,000 美元，第六週年及之後各週年時支付 35,000 美元。此外，Helio 適用未來銷售依賴性里程碑付款給 MEEI，總額最高為低七位數，以及根據淨銷售額百分比，為低單位數的 royalty 支付給 MEEI。Helio 也根據 MEEI 協議，需支付 MEEI 某些次授權收入的百分比，該百分比根據次授權日期從低雙位數降至中單位數。在我們收購 Helio 後，我們成為有義務支付 Helio 過去欠 MEEI 的任何未來付款。MEEI 協議下無其他股權對價需發行。

headings: 業務相關風險總覽
與 Reproxalap 及我們產品候選藥物潛在開發與商業化相關的風險
若我們未能開發及商業化其他產品候選藥物，我們可能無法擴大業務規模。
由於本公司在商業化藥物產品方面沒有經驗，因此關於我們產品候選藥物及業務前景的資訊有限。
我們可能無法成功識別或發現其他潛在產品候選藥物，或我們對某些產品候選藥物優先開發的決定，後續可能被證明是錯誤的。
為維護試驗的完整性，適應性臨牀試驗的初期部分之臨牀資料可能不會公開。
paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨許多風險。您應仔細考量下列所描述的風險，並配合本年度10-K表報表中其他資訊，這些風險可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況及未來成果造成重大影響。下列所描述的風險並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他未知或目前認為不重要之風險與不確定性，也可能對本公司業務、前景、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
